tasks.title: Durable job queue (lease/heartbeat/reclaim, window-aware, priority, cap)

prep.what: Build a persistent job queue with lease/heartbeat/reclaim mechanics, window-aware scheduling, priority ordering, and a concurrency cap.
prep.understand: The sweeper dispatches work today but has no durability — jobs lost on crash, no priority ordering, no window awareness. A lease+heartbeat model means each job is 'owned' for a short window; if the owner stops heartbeating, a reclaim cron resets it to pending. Window-awareness means jobs only fire when the 5h agent processing window is open. This is the prerequisite for t21 (the actual sweeper) to run reliably.
approach: Design the `jobs` DB table: id, status, priority, payload, leased_until, worker_id, attempts, max_attempts, window_tag, created_at.
Build `claimJob()` with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` — atomically sets status='claimed' + leased_until=now+30s; cap check: COUNT WHERE status='claimed' < MAX_CONCURRENT before claim.
Add `heartbeatJob(id)` (refreshes leased_until) and a reclaim cron that resets timed-out leases (leased_until < now AND status='claimed') back to 'pending'.
Wire into the existing triage/dispatch path — find where jobs are currently enqueued (the in-process queue) and replace with durable enqueue.
resources: Postgres `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` docs (single-consumer atomic claim without advisory locks)
todos_platform DB schema (db/migrations/) for the right migration baseline
Existing sweeper dispatch code — look for where triage results are currently enqueued

tasks.title: Unprivileged CI lane + sensitive-path human gate

prep.what: Create a GitHub Actions CI workflow that runs without secrets access, plus a required human-approval gate for PRs touching auth or deploy paths.
prep.understand: `pull_request_target` runs in the BASE repo's secret context — a supply-chain attack vector where a malicious fork PR can exfiltrate secrets. The safe pattern is `on: pull_request` (untrusted fork's SHA, zero secrets). Sensitive paths (auth/, migrations/, .env*, deploy/) need a separate gate workflow that posts a required status check blocking merge until a human explicitly approves via environment protection.
approach: Create `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with `on: pull_request` (NOT pull_request_target), NO secrets in env, running `bun test` + `tsc --noEmit` + lint.

Create `.github/workflows/sensitive-gate.yml` with `on: pull_request` and `paths:` filter covering auth/, db/migrations/, .env*, deploy/; posts a required 'sensitive-path-review' status check using a protected environment that needs a reviewer.
Add branch protection on main: require CI + sensitive-gate checks; no bypasses except repo admins.
Smoke-test by opening a draft PR touching an auth file — verify the gate fires and blocks merge.
resources: GitHub Actions `pull_request` vs `pull_request_target` security docs
Existing package.json scripts (test, build, lint commands to wire into CI)
GitHub environment protection rules (Settings > Environments) for the review gate

tasks.title: Daemon-side cross-process refresh lock (prereq for live SWEEPER_REPOS)
tasks.notes: The refresh CLI uses O_EXCL per-repo lockfile (CLI-vs-CLI only). Daemon's per-job lock is in-process and invisible to the CLI. Until fixed: run refresh ONLY while sweeper is stopped.

prep.what: Make the sweeper daemon acquire the same per-repo O_EXCL lockfile the refresh CLI uses, preventing a manual refresh and a daemon job from operating on the same repo simultaneously.
prep.understand: The CLI uses `O_EXCL` (open-exclusive — fails atomically if file exists) as a single-flight mutex per repo. The daemon has its own in-process per-job lock, but file locks from different processes are invisible to each other. Right now, running `refresh` while the daemon is mid-job means two processes can modify the same repo simultaneously — corrupted workspace or lost work. This is the last safety gate before you can point the sweeper at real repos.
approach: Find the CLI's per-repo lockfile path (e.g. `SWEEPER_STATE_DIR/<repo-slug>.lock`) and the O_EXCL open logic in `refreshRepo`.
In the daemon's job-start path, open the same lockfile with `fs.open(lockPath, 'wx')` (O_EXCL equivalent in Node); on EEXIST → set job status='deferred', requeue with 30s backoff.
Wrap the job's full lifecycle in try/finally that closes + `fs.unlink`s the lockfile on both success and error (no leaked locks).
Add a test: start a daemon job, fire CLI refresh for the same repo, assert CLI gets EEXIST and exits cleanly rather than double-refreshing.
resources: Node.js `fs.open` with `'wx'` flag (write-exclusive, equivalent to O_CREAT|O_EXCL)
Existing CLI `refreshRepo` lockfile code (SWEEPER_STATE_DIR path and O_EXCL logic)
Daemon job runner — the state transition from 'claimed' → 'running' is where the lock goes in
advisor-logs/2026-07-19-freshness-hardening.md for the overall refresh-lock design context

prep.what: Finish the 3-tier agency authorization layer: add AgencyRole runtime validation, denormalize agencyId onto every agent-facing model, enforce the cross-agency invariant, and write isolation tests.
prep.understand: The DB scaffold is done (Agency, AgencyMembership, Tenant.agencyId, provisionAgencyOfOne — all in commit fd6c8e1). What's missing is RUNTIME enforcement. Every agent-owned row needs a denormalized `agencyId` alongside `tenantId` so agency-level rollups work without joins — and so the `$allOperations` middleware can enforce the cross-agency invariant (child.agencyId == parent.agencyId). Without this, an agent query scoped to tenant B could populate agency A's rollup view.
approach: Add `agencyId BigInt` to every agent-facing Prisma model + new migration; add cross-agency invariant check in `$allOperations` middleware (throw if child.agencyId != resolved parent.agencyId).

Build `assertAgencyMember(agencyId, userId, minRole: AgencyRole)`: resolve AgencyMembership row, validate AgencyRole against a Zod enum (runtime — not just TS types), throw 403 on role mismatch or missing membership.
Wire `assertAgencyMember` into every route/action that touches cross-tenant or agency-level resources (look for any action that reads across tenantIds).

Add agency-isolation tests: provision agency A (tenantA1, tenantA2) and agency B (tenantB1); verify `db` scoped to tenantA1 cannot read agency B's agent models — mirror the test:tenants pattern (13 assertions).

tasks.title: pending_outbound approval state machine + DB guard
tasks.notes: DONE: PendingOutbound model (approvalTokenHash/expiresAt/consumedAt/approvedByUserId FK), DB CHECKs, queueForApproval, assertDispatchable (7 tests green). REMAINING: approve/decline/expire transitions, one-time token consumption, claim→deliver→mark-sent worker.

prep.what: Wire the approve/decline/expire HTTP endpoints with one-time token consumption, then add the Inngest worker that claims an approved item, delivers via ChannelRouter, and marks it sent.
prep.understand: The foundation is solid (PendingOutbound shape, DB CHECKs, queueForApproval, assertDispatchable — 7 tests green in commit f8740ce). Missing pieces: the state transition endpoints and the delivery worker. Key invariant: a token is ONE-TIME (consumedAt prevents replay attacks), expiry must be checked AT CLAIM TIME not just at creation, and `ChannelRouter.send` must be the ONLY place that does external delivery — no direct-send shortcuts.
approach: Add POST `/api/outbound/approve?token=...`: hash the incoming token (SHA-256), look up PendingOutbound WHERE approvalTokenHash=hash AND consumedAt IS NULL AND expiresAt > NOW(); set consumedAt=now, approvedByUserId=session.userId, emit `outbound.approved` Inngest event.
Add POST `/api/outbound/decline?token=...`: same token lookup, set status='declined'.
Add Inngest cron (hourly): `UPDATE PendingOutbound SET status='expired' WHERE status='pending' AND expiresAt < NOW()`.
Add Inngest handler on `outbound.approved`: call `assertDispatchable` → `ChannelRouter.send` → set status='sent'; on retry-exhaustion set status='failed' + operator alert.
resources: Existing PendingOutbound model + `queueForApproval` + `assertDispatchable` (test:outbound 7 checks — don't break these)
ChannelRouter interface (the only external-send seam — locate in lib/)
Inngest `onUserCreated` function as the pattern for adding new Inngest functions
DB CHECKs (external+sent=>approvedAt; status value set) — new migrations must not violate these constraints
